work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Philippenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI PRIMI : PAULUS ET TIMOTHEUS SERVI JESU CHRISTI.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ.

paras.t: Personas salutantes tangit Apostolus Paulus et Timotheus servi Jesu Christi, non servitute timorosa et pure servili, sed amorosa ac libera. Non addit Paulus hoc loco nomen gloriæ suæ ac summæ dignitatis, dicendo : Paulus apostolus, etc., quoniam Philippenses nihil indignum de ipso senserunt. Conjungit quoque Apostolus sibi Timotheum, quamvis ipse solus epistolam dictaverit, quia missurus erat eum ad Philippenses. Unde ut reverentius eum susciperent, diligentiusque audirent, exprimit eum in forma salutationis. Hi ergo mandant omnibus sanctis, id est vere fidelibus, in Christo Jesu, id est per fidem, caritatem et gratiam Christi, qui sunt, id est commorantur, Philippis, id est in urbe Macedoniæ, quæ est pars Græciæ : quam urbem construxit Philippus pater Alexandri Magni putativus, vocans eam ex nomine suo Philippos ; cum episcopis et diaconibus, id est, etiam episcopis atque diaconis mandant. Hi enim tanquam principales, post generalem omnium designationem exprimuntur. Porro, ut Haymo asserit, per episcopos intelliguntur presbyteri. Non enim in una urbe plures episcopi præsidebant ; nec ab episcopis ad diaconos descenderet, prætermissis presbyteris, nisi per episcopos intelligeret sacerdotes. Unde dici solet, quod in primitiva Ecclesia episcopi non distinguebantur a sacerdotibus. Episcopus namque dicitur, quasi supra intentus, ab ἐπί, quod est supra, et σκοπός, intentio : sed hoc episcopis convenit atque presbyteris. Unde hoc loco per episcopos presbyteri, et summus eorum, videlicet pontifex Philippensium, intelliguntur.
paras.en: The Apostle touches on the persons who send the greeting: [[1:1|Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ|Paulus et Timotheus servi Jesu Christi]], not with a fearful and merely servile servitude, but with one that is loving and free. Paul does not add here the name of his glory and highest dignity, saying, Paul an apostle, etc., since the Philippians thought nothing unworthy of him. The Apostle also joins Timothy with himself, although he alone dictated the epistle, because he was about to send him to the Philippians. So, that they might receive him with more reverence and hear him more attentively, he names him in the form of greeting. These, then, send greeting [[1:1|to all the saints|omnibus sanctis]], that is, to the truly faithful, [[1:1|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the faith, charity and grace of Christ, [[1:1|who are|qui sunt]], that is, who dwell, [[1:1|at Philippi|Philippis]], that is, in a city of Macedonia, which is part of Greece: a city which Philip, the reputed father of Alexander the Great, built, calling it Philippi after his own name; [[1:1|with the bishops and deacons|cum episcopis et diaconibus]]: that is, they send greeting to the bishops and deacons as well. For these, as the chief ones, are named after the general mention of all. Further, as Haymo asserts, by bishops are understood priests [presbyteri, the elders of the Church]. For several bishops did not preside in one city; nor would he go down from bishops to deacons, passing over the priests, unless by bishops he meant priests. Hence it is commonly said that in the primitive Church bishops were not distinguished from priests. For a bishop (episcopus) is so called as being intent above, from ἐπί, which means above, and σκοπός, intent [that is, one who watches over others: an overseer]: but this fits bishops and priests alike. Hence here by bishops are understood the priests, and the highest of them, namely the bishop of the Philippians.

paras.t: Gratia gratificans detur et insit vobis et pax interior, quæ est tranquillitas mentis, atque exterior, quæ est quies ab extrinseco impugnante, a Deo Patre nostro, id est persona Patris æterni, et Domino Jesu Christo : quibus expressis, intelligitur Spiritus Sanctus, amor et nexus amborum : qui omnes sunt una fontalis et effectiva origo totius bonitatis creatæ.
paras.en: [[1:2|Grace|Gratia]], the grace that makes pleasing [gratia gratificans: sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God], be given and abide [[1:2|unto you and peace|vobis et pax]]: inward peace, which is tranquillity of mind, and outward peace, which is rest from one who assails from without; [[1:2|from God our Father|a Deo Patre nostro]], that is, from the person of the eternal Father, [[1:2|and from the Lord Jesus Christ|et Domino Jesu Christo]]: and with these named, the Holy Ghost is understood, the love and bond of both; and all of them are one fountain-like and effective origin of all created goodness.

paras.t: Gratias ago Deo meo, id est superbeatissimæ Trinitati, simplicissimo Deo, qui est omnium Deus generaliter, et Deus meus specialiter, propter specialem pietatem, gratiam et providentiam ejus in me, et item propter singularem dilectionem et cultum quibus ei soli principaliter finaliterque inhæreo. Hoc dicere non competit nisi perfectis. Propter quod divinus et magnus Dionysius, hoc dicere vix præsumens, interdum sic ait : Deus, et si fas est dicere, meus. In omni memoria vestri semper, id est toties quoties vestri memor sum, in cunctis orationibus meis fusis pro omnibus vobis. Dum enim memor sum vestri, occurrit mihi consideratio gratiæ exsistentis in vobis : de qua grates refero ; et oro ut gratia ampliori mereamini adimpleri.
paras.en: [[1:3|I give thanks to my God|Gratias ago Deo meo]], that is, to the most supremely blessed Trinity, the most simple God, who is the God of all in general, and my God in particular, because of his special loving-kindness, grace and providence towards me, and also because of the singular love and worship by which I cleave to him alone as my chief and final end. To say this befits none but the perfect. For which reason the divine and great Dionysius [the Areopagite], scarcely presuming to say it, speaks thus at times: God, and, if it be lawful to say it, mine. [[1:3|in every remembrance of you|In omni memoria vestri]] [[1:4|Always|semper]], that is, as often as I am mindful of you, [[1:4|in all my prayers|in cunctis orationibus meis]] poured out [[1:4|for you all|pro omnibus vobis]]. For whenever I am mindful of you, there comes to me the thought of the grace that is in you: for which I return thanks; and I pray that you may deserve to be filled with more abundant grace.

paras.t: Cum gaudio spirituali deprecationem faciens, id est, Deum pro vobis exorans : gaudio, inquam, concepto seu habito super communicatione vestra, id est de beneficio vobis concesso, videlicet quod mihi communicastis seu conformati estis fide, caritate et opere, in Evangelio Christi, id est in prædicatione, exhortatione, seu observatione evangelicæ legis, a prima die conversionis vestræ usque nunc ; confidens hoc ipsum, id est, ex consideratione gratiæ vobis hucusque concessæ, confido de gratia pleniori, videlicet quia, id est quod, qui cœpit in vobis opus bonum, id est Deus qui per gratiam gratum facientem, et Spiritus Sancti motionem actualem, inchoavit in vobis opus meritorium, perficiet illud in vobis usque in diem Jesu Christi inclusive, id est usque in diem mortis vestræ, qua a Christo visitabimini, et particulare judicium sustinebitis. A Deo enim est inchoatio, continuatio et consummatio operis boni.
paras.en: [[1:4|making supplication|deprecationem faciens]] [[1:4|with joy|Cum gaudio]], spiritual joy, that is, entreating God for you: with joy, I say, conceived or had [[1:5|For your communication|super communicatione vestra]], that is, for the benefit granted to you, namely that you have shared with me, or been made like me, in faith, charity and work, [[1:5|in the gospel of Christ|in Evangelio Christi]], that is, in the preaching, exhortation or observance of the law of the gospel, [[1:5|from the first day|a prima die]] of your conversion [[1:5|unto now|usque nunc]]; [[1:6|Being confident of this very thing|confidens hoc ipsum]], that is, from considering the grace granted to you hitherto, I am confident of a fuller grace, namely [[1:6|that|quia]] [Denis glosses quia, which can mean because, as quod, that] [[1:6|he who hath begun a good work in you|qui cœpit in vobis opus bonum]], that is, God, who by sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes one pleasing to God] and the actual motion of the Holy Ghost has begun in you meritorious work, [[1:6|will perfect it|perficiet]] in you [[1:6|unto the day of Christ Jesus|usque in diem Jesu Christi]] inclusive, that is, until the day of your death, when you will be visited by Christ and will undergo the particular judgment. For from God are the beginning, the continuing and the completion of a good work.

paras.t: Sicut est mihi justum hoc sentire pro omnibus vobis, id est, tam ex parte divinæ bonitatis, quam ex parte vestræ stabilitatis, justum est ut ita confidam de et pro vobis, videlicet quod Deus perficiet in vobis opus bonum a se inchoatum ; eo quod habeam vos in corde, id est, cordiali affectu hoc optem et sperem quod subditur : et in vinculis meis, et in defensione et confirmatione Evangelii, socios gaudii mei omnes vos esse, id est, ut tam in præsenti quam in futuro, sitis participes consolationis meæ internæ : quam habeo in vinculis meis, quibus propter Evangelii prædicationem ligatus sum ; et in defensione Evangelii, qua evangelicam veritatem defendo contra adversarios ejus ; et confirmatione Evangelii, qua illud confirmo, instanter et imperterrite prædicando, miracula faciendo, Scripturarum testimonia allegando, irreprehensibiliter conversando. Quam etiam consolationem multo copiosius habebo in patria pro vinculis atque laboribus istis. Vel, ideo hæc dicit Apostolus, quoniam Philippenses socii fuerunt gaudii ejus in vinculis, etc., ita quod ipsi quoque pro Christo vincula pertulerunt, et Evangelium defenderunt atque constanter prædicaverunt sive professi sunt.
paras.en: [[1:7|As it is meet for me to think this for you all|Sicut est mihi justum hoc sentire pro omnibus vobis]], that is, it is just, as much on the part of the divine goodness as on the part of your steadfastness, that I should be thus confident of you and for you, namely that God will perfect in you the good work he has begun; [[1:7|for that I have you in my heart|eo quod habeam vos in corde]], that is, with heartfelt affection I wish and hope for what is added: [[1:7|and that, in my bands and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, you all are partakers of my joy|et in vinculis meis, et in defensione et confirmatione Evangelii, socios gaudii mei omnes vos esse]], that is, that both in the present and in the future you may be partakers of my inward consolation, which I have in my bands, with which I am bound for the preaching of the gospel; and in the defence of the gospel, by which I defend the truth of the gospel against its adversaries; and in the confirmation of the gospel, by which I confirm it, by preaching urgently and fearlessly, working miracles, bringing forward the testimonies of the Scriptures, and living blamelessly. And this consolation I shall have far more abundantly in the fatherland [that is, in heaven] for these bands and labours. Or else the Apostle says this because the Philippians were partakers of his joy in bands, etc., in that they too bore bands for Christ, and defended the gospel and steadfastly preached or professed it.

paras.t: Testis enim mihi est Deus, quomodo, id est quam affectuose, spiritualiter et sincere, cupiam omnes vos, id est, omnium vestrum salutem et communionem cum gaudio meo desiderem : et hoc, in visceribus Jesu Christi, id est Christi amore, non humano affectu. Vel, Quomodo cupiam vos esse in visceribus Jesu Christi, id est Christo intime uniri, atque ab eo cordialiter diligi.
paras.en: [[1:8|For God is my witness|Testis enim mihi est Deus]], [[1:8|how|quomodo]], that is, how affectionately, spiritually and sincerely, [[1:8|I long after you all|cupiam omnes vos]], that is, how I desire the salvation of you all and your fellowship in my joy: and this [[1:8|in the bowels of Jesus Christ|in visceribus Jesu Christi]], that is, with the love of Christ, not with human affection. Or: how I long for you to be in the bowels of Jesus Christ, that is, to be inwardly united to Christ and loved by him from the heart.

paras.t: Et hoc oro Deum, ut caritas vestra vobis a Deo infusa, qua Deum proximumque meritorie diligitis, magis ac magis abundet, id est, incessanter proficiat, in scientia, id est discretione, ut omnia discrete agatis, sitque rationabile obsequium vestrum ; vel, In scientia, id est, quatenus diligendo mereamini illuminari a Deo in cognitione divinorum ac aliorum ; vel, In scientia illa quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, de qua ait Scriptura, Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum : per quam habet homo rectum judicium de rebus creatis, videlicet quod eis non sit finaliter inhærendum, eo quod ex se vanæ sint atque caducæ. Et in omni sensu, id est intellectuali notitia, vel potius experimentali gustu, eorum quæ ad salutem exiguntur.
paras.en: [[1:9|And this I pray|Et hoc oro]] to God, [[1:9|That your charity|ut caritas vestra]], infused into you by God, by which you love God and your neighbour meritoriously, [[1:9|may more and more abound|magis ac magis abundet]], that is, may advance unceasingly, [[1:9|in knowledge|in scientia]], that is, in discretion, so that you may do all things with discretion, and that it may be [[Rom 12:1|your reasonable service|rationabile obsequium vestrum]]; or, In knowledge, that is, so that by loving you may deserve to be enlightened by God in the knowledge of divine and other things; or, In that knowledge which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], of which Scripture says: [[Wis 10:10|gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum]]; by which a man has right judgment about created things, namely that he is not to cleave to them as to his end, since of themselves they are vain and perishable. [[1:9|and in all understanding|Et in omni sensu]], that is, in intellectual knowledge, or rather in the experienced taste, of the things that are required for salvation.

paras.t: Ut probetis, id est, approbando sequamini, potiora, id est opera perfectiora, in dies magis proficiendo, ut sitis sinceri, id est mundi corde. Beati etenim mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt. Unde in Proverbiis habetur : Qui diligit cordis munditiam, habebit amicum regem. Et sine offensa, id est sine opere malo, præsertim mortali, et ne perseveretis in aliquo vitio, quatenus nec Deum nec proximum offendatis, quantum fieri potest, in diem Christi, id est perseveranter usque ad mortem. Repleti fructu, id est actu et delectatione, justitiæ : quæ est præclarissima virtus; et nec Lucifer, nec Hesperus est ita admirabilis, teste Philosopho. Repleti, inquam, non propriis viribus, sed per Jesum Christum, id est virtute et merito Christi, in gloriam et laudem Dei, id est propter hoc ut Deus glorificetur atque laudetur a vobis, aliisque electis in præsenti et in futuro.
paras.en: [[1:10|That you may approve|Ut probetis]], that is, may approve and follow, [[1:10|the better things|potiora]], that is, more perfect works, advancing more from day to day; [[1:10|that you may be sincere|ut sitis sinceri]], that is, clean of heart. For [[Matt 5:8|Blessed|Beati]] indeed [[Matt 5:8|are the clean of heart: they shall see God|mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]. Hence we have in Proverbs: [[Prov 22:11|He that loveth cleanness of heart|Qui diligit cordis munditiam]], [[Prov 22:11|shall have the king for his friend|habebit amicum regem]] [the margin gives Prov. xi; the words are from Prov 22:11]. [[1:10|and without offence|Et sine offensa]], that is, without evil work, especially mortal, and so that you do not persevere in any vice, so as to offend neither God nor your neighbour, as far as may be, [[1:10|unto the day of Christ|in diem Christi]], that is, perseveringly until death. [[1:11|Filled with the fruit|Repleti fructu]], that is, with the act and the delight, [[1:11|of justice|justitiæ]]: which is a most glorious virtue; and neither Lucifer nor Hesperus [the morning star and the evening star] is so wonderful, as the Philosopher testifies [Aristotle, Ethics V]. Filled, I say, not by your own powers, but [[1:11|through Jesus Christ|per Jesum Christum]], that is, by the power and merit of Christ, [[1:11|unto the glory and praise of God|in gloriam et laudem Dei]], that is, to this end, that God may be glorified and praised by you and by the other elect, in the present and in the future.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus efficit Philippenses benevolos, statum suum eis insinuans tanquam familiaribus et amicis præcipuis. Scire autem volo vos, fratres, quia quæ circa me sunt, id est tribulationes, incarcerationes et vincula quæ mihi acciderunt, magis ad profectum, id est publicationem, confirmationem ac venerationem, Evangelii venerunt, quam ad detrimentum ipsius : et hoc, contra intentionem persecutorum meorum, qui ideo me vinxerunt, ut Evangelium obfuscaretur : ita ut vincula mea manifesta fierent, id est, captivitas mea et fructus vinculorum meorum divulgaretur, in Christo, id est secundum voluntatem ac dispositionem Christi, vel ad gloriam ejus, in omni prætorio judicum, quo majores conveniunt, non solum Romæ, sed in prætoriis quoque urbium aliarum, et in ceteris omnibus locis judicialibus quo minores concurrunt. Ut enim Haymo dicit, quum Apostolus retrusus esset in carcerem in domo imperatoris, multa fecit prodigia, et in carcere vinctis et aliis advenientibus constantissime prædicavit, sicque convertit quamplurimos, ita ut et de palatio imperatoris faceret ecclesiam Redemptoris. Quum vero in prætorium duceretur, efficacissime et cum summa securitate respondit. Quoniam ergo Roma caput exstitit mundi, fideles qui Romam confluxerunt et exierunt, ubique retulerunt signa, fructum atque constantiam Pauli. Quo audito, complures animati fuerunt ad evangelizandum, sicut adjungitur.
paras.en: Next the Apostle makes the Philippians well disposed, making known his state to them as to intimates and special friends. [[1:12|Now, brethren, I desire you should know|Scire autem volo vos, fratres]], [[1:12|that the things which have happened to me|quia quæ circa me sunt]], that is, the tribulations, imprisonments and bands that have befallen me, [[1:12|have fallen out rather to the furtherance|magis ad profectum]], that is, to the spreading, strengthening and honouring, [[1:12|of the gospel|Evangelii venerunt]], than to its harm: and this against the intention of my persecutors, who bound me so that the gospel might be darkened: [[1:13|So that my bands are made manifest|ita ut vincula mea manifesta fierent]], that is, so that my captivity and the fruit of my bands might be spread abroad, [[1:13|in Christ|in Christo]], that is, according to the will and disposition of Christ, or to his glory, [[1:13|in all the court|in omni prætorio]] [prætorium, the judgment hall] of the judges, where the greater people gather, not only at Rome but in the courts of other cities as well, [[1:13|and in all other places|et in ceteris omnibus]] of judgment, where the lesser people come together. For, as Haymo says, when the Apostle had been thrust into prison in the emperor's house, he worked many wonders, and in prison preached most steadfastly to those in chains and to others who came to him, and so converted a great many, so that he made even of the emperor's palace a church of the Redeemer. And when he was led into the court, he answered most effectively and with the greatest assurance. Since, then, Rome was the head of the world, the faithful who flocked to Rome and went out from it reported everywhere the signs, the fruit and the steadfastness of Paul. Hearing this, very many were emboldened to preach the gospel, as is added.

paras.t: Ut plures e fratribus in Domino confidentes, non in se ipsis, vinculis meis, id est occasione seu intuitu vinculorum meorum, hoc est exemplo meo, abundantius quam ante auderent sine timore eorum qui corpus occidunt, verbum Dei loqui, id est Christi Evangelium prædicare, dicentes : Si magister noster in vinculis, in carcere, in prætorio prædicat sine pavore, cur nos libere euntes, a prædicatione cessamus?
paras.en: So that [[1:14|many of the brethren in the Lord, growing confident|plures e fratribus in Domino confidentes]], not in themselves, [[1:14|by my bands|vinculis meis]], that is, on the occasion or at the sight of my bands, that is, by my example, [[1:14|are much more bold|abundantius quam ante auderent]] than before, [[1:14|without fear|sine timore]] of [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|qui corpus occidunt]], [[1:14|to speak the word of God|verbum Dei loqui]], that is, to preach the Gospel of Christ, saying: If our master preaches without dread in bands, in prison, in the court, why do we, who go about free, cease from preaching?

paras.t: Quidam quidem, id est nonnulli a prædictis virtuosis diversi, et propter invidiam et contentionem, id est ex invidia qua invident gloriæ apostolatus mei, eumque habere contendunt, quidam autem, et propter bonam voluntatem, id est recta intentione et ex dilectione Dei ac proximi, Christum prædicant ut proximi consequantur salutem, et Christi honor augeatur. Quidam autem boni, ex caritate speciali ad me hoc faciunt, vicem meam supplentes, scientes hoc, scilicet, quoniam, id est quod, in defensione Evangelii, id est ad defendendum evangelicæ veritatis prædicationem, positus sum in gradu et gratia apostolatus a Deo; vel, In (id est pro) defensione Evangelii positus sum in carcere. Quidam autem ex contentione Christum annuntiant, id est, qui mecum contenderunt, atque a me confutati, et prædicationis officio indigni judicati sunt, non sincere, id est, non pura hoc agunt intentione, existimantes pressuram se suscitare, id est tribulationis augmentum procurare, vinculis meis, id est mihi vincto, concitando alios contra me, quasi contra principalem doctorem hujus legis : videlicet, ut si quis velit eos affligere propter prædicationem Evangelii, concitent eum adversum me, velut contra præcipuam causam prædicationis hujusmodi. Vel, Existimantes pressuram se suscitare vinculis meis, id est me vinctum contristare ac tribulare, eo quod prædicent non obstante quod ego reprobaverim eos.
paras.en: [[1:15|Some indeed|Quidam quidem]], that is, certain men unlike the virtuous ones just spoken of, [[1:15|even out of envy and contention|et propter invidiam et contentionem]], that is, out of envy, with which they envy the glory of my apostleship and strive to have it; [[1:15|but some also for good will|quidam autem, et propter bonam voluntatem]], that is, with right intention and out of love of God and of their neighbour, [[1:15|preach Christ|Christum prædicant]], that their neighbours may obtain salvation and the honour of Christ be increased. [[1:16|Some|Quidam autem]] good men do this [[1:16|out of charity|ex caritate]] that is special towards me, taking my place, [[1:16|knowing|scientes]] this, namely, [[1:16|that|quoniam]] [Denis glosses quoniam as quod, that] [[1:16|I am set|positus sum]] [[1:16|for the defence of the gospel|in defensione Evangelii]], that is, to defend the preaching of the gospel truth, set by God in the rank and grace of the apostleship; or, I am set in (that is, for) the defence of the gospel in prison. [[1:17|And some out of contention|Quidam autem ex contentione]] [[1:17|preach Christ|Christum annuntiant]], that is, those who contended with me and, being refuted by me, were judged unworthy of the office of preaching, [[1:17|not sincerely|non sincere]], that is, they do this with no pure intention, [[1:17|supposing that they raise affliction|existimantes pressuram se suscitare]], that is, that they bring about an increase of tribulation, [[1:17|to my bands|vinculis meis]], that is, to me in bands, by stirring up others against me as against the chief teacher of this law: namely, so that if anyone wishes to afflict them for preaching the gospel, they may stir him up against me, as against the chief cause of such preaching. Or, Supposing that they raise affliction to my bands, that is, that they sadden and trouble me in my bands, because they preach notwithstanding that I have rejected them.

paras.t: Quid enim? id est, quid interest, vel quid mihi curandum est de tanta diversitate prædicantium? Dum omnimodo, id est omnibus modis, sive per occasionem, id est incidentaliter, scilicet ex invidia seu contentione, sive per veritatem, id est ex vera et recta intentione, Christus annuntietur : et in hoc gaudeo quod sic est, sed et gaudebo inde de cetero ; vel, Gaudeo in via, et gaudebo in patria.
paras.en: [[1:18|But what then?|Quid enim?]] that is, what does it matter, or what need I care about so great a diversity of preachers? [[1:18|So that by all means|Dum omnimodo]], that is, in every way, [[1:18|whether by occasion|sive per occasionem]], that is, incidentally, namely out of envy or contention, [[1:18|or by truth|sive per veritatem]], that is, out of a true and right intention, [[1:18|Christ be preached|Christus annuntietur]]: [[1:18|in this also I rejoice|et in hoc gaudeo]], that it is so, [[1:18|yea, and will rejoice|sed et gaudebo]] in it from now on; or, I rejoice on the way, and I shall rejoice in the fatherland [that is, in this life, and in heaven].

paras.t: Scio enim quia hoc, videlicet quod Christus omnimodo annuntiatur occasione mei, mihi proveniet ad salutem æternam, id est, causa majoris gloriæ erit mihi in patria, non dumtaxat meritis meis, sed et per vestram orationem fusam pro me, et subministrationem, id est sustentationem et opem, Spiritus Jesu Christi, id est Spiritus Sancti a Christo procedentis : qui Spiritus adjuvat nostram infirmitatem, nosque in bono, ne ruamus, sustentat, sicut columna fulcit structuram. Si autem subministratio videatur non competere Sancto Spiritui, poterit per spiritum Christi intelligi spiritus angelicus missus a Christo : qui utique nostræ cooperatur saluti, quum simus ejus custodiæ deputati.
paras.en: [[1:19|For I know that this|Scio enim quia hoc]], namely that Christ is in every way preached on my account, [[1:19|shall fall out to me unto salvation|mihi proveniet ad salutem]] eternal, that is, it will be the cause of greater glory for me in the fatherland, not only through my own merits, but also [[1:19|through your prayer|per vestram orationem]] poured out for me, [[1:19|and the supply|et subministrationem]], that is, the support and help, [[1:19|of the Spirit of Jesus Christ|Spiritus Jesu Christi]], that is, of the Holy Ghost proceeding from Christ: which Spirit helps our infirmity and holds us up in good, lest we fall, as a column props up a building. But if supply should seem not to befit the Holy Ghost, by the spirit of Christ may be understood an angelic spirit sent by Christ, who indeed works together for our salvation, since we are given into his keeping.

paras.t: Sic autem proveniet mihi secundum exspectationem actualem et spem meam habitualem, id est, quemadmodum spero, vel tam copiose sicut confido, quia in nullo loco, tempore, seu eventu, confundar ita sperando. Spes enim non confundit, juxta illud in Psalmo : Universi qui sustinent te, non confundentur ; in Ecclesiastico quoque, Scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est. Sed in omni fiducia, id est cum ingenti confidentia cordis mei in Deo, sicut semper ab exordio conversionis meæ magnificatus est : ita et nunc ultra, quamdiu subsisto in carne, magnificabitur, id est honorabitur, Christus in corpore meo, id est in actionibus et passionibus corporis mei, sive per vitam, sive per mortem, id est in vita ac morte : quia si vixero, honorabo Christum prædicando; si occidor aut morior, exemplum deferendo.
paras.en: And so it shall fall out to me [[1:20|According to my expectation|secundum exspectationem]], my actual expectation, [[1:20|and hope|et spem meam]], my habitual hope [Denis distinguishes the act of hoping from hope as an abiding virtue], that is, as I hope, or as abundantly as I trust, [[1:20|that in nothing|quia in nullo]], no place, time or event, [[1:20|I shall be confounded|confundar]] in hoping thus. For [[Rom 5:5|hope confoundeth not|Spes enim non confundit]] [the margin gives Ibid. v, 5, though the note before it is Matth. x, 28; the words are Rom 5:5], according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 24:3|none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded|Universi qui sustinent te, non confundentur]]; and in Ecclesiasticus too: [[Ecclus 2:11|know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|Scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est]]. [[1:20|but with all confidence|Sed in omni fiducia]], that is, with great trust of my heart in God, [[1:20|as always|sicut semper]] from the beginning of my conversion he has been magnified, [[1:20|so now also|ita et nunc]], from now on, as long as I remain in the flesh, [[1:20|shall Christ be magnified|magnificabitur]], that is, honoured, [[1:20|in my body|in corpore meo]], that is, in the actions and sufferings of my body, [[1:20|whether it be by life or by death|sive per vitam, sive per mortem]], that is, in life and in death: for if I live, I shall honour Christ by preaching; if I am slain or die, by giving an example.

paras.t: Mihi enim vivere in corpore isto, Christus est finaliter et meritorie, id est, ad Christum ordino vitam meam, eique uniri vivendo promereor. Ipse quoque est vita vivificans me effective, conservando et dando vitam naturæ ac gratiæ. Unde in Evangelio : Ego, inquit, sum via, veritas et vita. Et in Deuteronomio aiebat Moyses : Ipse est vita tua et longitudo dierum tuorum. Et mori est mihi lucrum, id est æternæ vitæ meritorium seu beatitudinis ostium.
paras.en: [[1:21|For to me, to live|Mihi enim vivere]] in this body [[1:21|is Christ|Christus est]], as end and by merit: that is, I order my life to Christ, and by living I merit to be united to him. He too is the life that gives me life, as its efficient cause, preserving and giving the life of nature and of grace. Hence in the Gospel: [[John 14:6|I|Ego]], he says, [[John 14:6|am the way, and the truth, and the life|sum via, veritas et vita]]. And in Deuteronomy Moses said: [[Deut 30:20|he is thy life, and the length of thy days|Ipse est vita tua et longitudo dierum tuorum]]. [[1:21|and to die is|Et mori est]] to me [[1:21|gain|lucrum]], that is, a means of meriting eternal life, or the gate of blessedness.

paras.t: Quod si vivere in carne, id est in corpore isto manere ac prædicare, hic mihi fructus operis est, id est, tam pretiosus et utilis fructus est conversationis in carne, ut dixi, videlicet quod semper magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, et mihi vivere Christus sit : si, inquam, hoc sic est, imo quia sic est, et quid eligam tanquam utilius, scilicet, vivere an mori, ignoro. Alias tamen indubitanter eligerem mori, ut possem esse præsens cum Christo. Coarctor autem e duobus, id est, duo coarctant me, scilicet desiderium dissolvendi, et necessitas in carne manendi. Inter hæc duo angustor, et ex consideratione ipsorum quasi in arcto constituor, utrumque desiderans, quum tamen simul haberi non queant, et quid electurus sim, nesciens. Consequenter tangit hæc duo : desiderium habens dissolvi a corpore et esse cum Christo principaliter per gloriam fruitionis ; multo enim magis melius est hoc, quam detineri in hac carne mortali. Permanere autem in carne, id est me diutius vivere in sæculo isto, necessarium, id est multum expediens est, propter vos, id est ad vestram pleniorem instructionem, confirmationem atque salutem.
paras.en: [[1:22|And if to live in the flesh|Quod si vivere in carne]], that is, to remain in this body and preach, [[1:22|this is to me the fruit of labour|hic mihi fructus operis est]], that is, so precious and profitable is the fruit of living in the flesh, as I have said, namely that Christ will always be magnified in my body, and that to me to live is Christ: if, I say, this is so, nay rather, since it is so, [[1:22|And what I shall choose|et quid eligam]] as the more profitable, namely to live or to die, [[1:22|I know not|ignoro]]. Otherwise, however, I should without doubt choose to die, so as to be present with Christ. [[1:23|But I am straitened between two|Coarctor autem e duobus]], that is, two things straiten me, namely the desire to be dissolved and the need to remain in the flesh. Between these two I am hard pressed, and in considering them I am set as it were in a strait, desiring both, though they cannot be had together, and not knowing which I shall choose. Next he touches on these two: [[1:23|having a desire to be dissolved|desiderium habens dissolvi]] from the body [[1:23|and to be with Christ|et esse cum Christo]], chiefly through the glory of fruition [that is, the enjoyment of God in heaven]; [[1:23|a thing by far the better|multo enim magis melius est hoc]] than to be held back in this mortal flesh. [[1:24|But to abide still in the flesh|Permanere autem in carne]], that is, that I should live longer in this world, [[1:24|is needful|necessarium]], that is, is very expedient, [[1:24|for you|propter vos]], that is, for your fuller instruction, strengthening and salvation.

paras.t: Et hoc confidens, scilicet quod necessarium est me in carne manere propter vos, confidens sic esse, scio ex revelatione divina seu magna fiducia, quia manebo et permanebo in vita præsenti omnibus vobis, ad profectum vestrum spiritualem, et gaudium fidei, id est propter consolationem vestram procedentem ex fide ; ut gratulatio vestra, id est interna exsultatio, abundet in Christo Jesu tanquam in objecto et causa, vel in consideratione beneficiorum ipsius, in me, id est per me, videlicet per liberationem mei de carcere, et prolongationem vitæ meæ ad vestrum profectum, per meum adventum iterum ad vos, quia tunc coram referam ipse vobis plenius, quæ jam breviter scribo.
paras.en: [[1:25|And having this confidence|Et hoc confidens]], namely that it is needful for me to remain in the flesh for your sake, being confident that it is so, [[1:25|I know|scio]] by divine revelation or by great trust [[1:25|that I shall abide and continue|quia manebo et permanebo]] in the present life [[1:25|with you all, for your furtherance|omnibus vobis, ad profectum vestrum]], your spiritual furtherance, [[1:25|and joy of faith|et gaudium fidei]], that is, for your consolation that proceeds from faith; [[1:26|That your rejoicing|ut gratulatio vestra]], that is, your inward exultation, [[1:26|may abound in Christ Jesus|abundet in Christo Jesu]] as in its object and cause, or in the consideration of his benefits, [[1:26|for me|in me]], that is, through me, namely through my release from prison and the lengthening of my life for your furtherance, [[1:26|by my coming to you again|per meum adventum iterum ad vos]]: for then I shall myself tell you more fully, face to face, what I now write briefly.

paras.t: Tantum digne Evangelio Christi conversamini, id est, hoc solum admoneo, ut tam sancte ac religiose vivatis ut exigit evangelica doctrina cui credidistis, quatenus (sicut alibi dictum est) digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis; ut sive quum venero et videro vos, sive absens exsistens a vobis, audiam de vobis a veridicis quod sequitur : quia statis, corde erecto per fidem et caritatem, in uno spiritu unanimes, id est in Spiritu Sancto concordes; vel, In uno spiritu creato, habentes cor unum et animam unam per caritatem ; collaborantes fidei Evangelii, id est, simul conantes implere fidei documenta. Et in nullo eventu terreamini ab adversariis, id est invisibilibus seu visibilibus hostibus, quæ perterritio seu molestia hostium, est illis causa perditionis, id est meritum condemnationis, quum sit mortale peccatum, vobis autem est causa salutis, quoniam eam patienter ferendo, meremini vitam æternam. Hinc quoque Salvator ait : Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere : et rursus alibi, Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Hoc est quod per Isaiam inducitur : Nolite timere opprobria hominum et blasphemias eorum. Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit?
paras.en: [[1:27|Only let your conversation be worthy of the gospel of Christ|Tantum digne Evangelio Christi conversamini]], that is, this alone I urge, that you live as holily and devoutly as the teaching of the gospel which you have believed requires, so that (as is said elsewhere) [[Eph 4:1|you walk worthy of the vocation in which you are called|digne ambuletis vocatione qua vocati estis]]; [[1:27|that, whether I come and see you|ut sive quum venero et videro vos]], [[1:27|or, being absent|sive absens]] from you, I [[1:27|may hear of you|audiam de vobis]] from truthful witnesses what follows: [[1:27|that you stand fast|quia statis]], with heart upright through faith and charity, [[1:27|in one spirit, with one mind|in uno spiritu unanimes]], that is, of one accord in the Holy Ghost; or, In one created spirit, having one heart and one soul through charity; [[1:27|labouring together for the faith of the gospel|collaborantes fidei Evangelii]], that is, striving together to fulfil the teachings of the faith. [[1:28|And in nothing|Et in nullo]] that befalls [[1:28|be ye terrified by the adversaries|terreamini ab adversariis]], that is, by enemies invisible or visible: which terrifying or harassment by the enemies [[1:28|to them is a cause of perdition|est illis causa perditionis]], that is, a desert of condemnation, since it is a mortal sin, [[1:28|but to you|vobis autem]] is a cause [[1:28|of salvation|salutis]], since by bearing it patiently you merit eternal life. Hence too the Saviour says: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere]]; and again elsewhere: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]]. This is what is set forth through Isaias: [[Is 51:7|fear ye not the reproach of men|Nolite timere opprobria hominum]], and [[Is 51:7|their blasphemies|blasphemias eorum]]. [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit?]]

paras.t: Et hoc a Deo, id est, non terreri et æquanimiter pati, Dei donum est, per gratiam ejus vobis collatum. Quia vobis gratiose donatum est a Deo trino ac uno pro Christo, id est propter meritum Christi, non solum ut in eum credatis, id est non sola fides ejusque actus interior, sed ut etiam pro illo patiamini, id est, virtus patientiæ, et ipsa sustinentia seu perpessio adversitatum, vobis a Deo concessa sunt, ita ut hæc inter munera Dei sint computanda : vobis, inquam, data sunt hæc, qui estis idem certamen, id est similem pugnam, habentes contra adversarios fidei, quale et vidistis in me, quando in Philippis cæsus sum, nudus atque incarceratus, eo quod spiritum malignum de muliere pythonissa excluserim (ut in Actibus legitur), et nunc quum Romæ ligatus sum, audistis de me.
paras.en: [[1:28|and this from God|Et hoc a Deo]], that is, not to be terrified, and to suffer with an even mind, is a gift of God, conferred on you by his grace. [[1:29|For unto you|Quia vobis]] graciously [[1:29|it is given|donatum est]] by God, three and one, [[1:29|for Christ|pro Christo]], that is, for the merit of Christ, [[1:29|not only to believe in him|non solum ut in eum credatis]], that is, not faith alone and its inward act, [[1:29|but also to suffer for him|sed ut etiam pro illo patiamini]], that is, the virtue of patience, and the very bearing or enduring of adversities, have been granted to you by God, so that these are to be counted among the gifts of God: to you, I say, these are given, who are [[1:30|Having the same conflict|idem certamen]], that is, a like fight, against the adversaries of the faith, [[1:30|as that which you have seen in me|quale et vidistis in me]], when at Philippi I was beaten, stripped[[Acts 16:22||]] and imprisoned[[Acts 16:23||]], because I had cast the evil spirit out of a woman with a pythonical spirit[[Acts 16:18||]] (as we read in the Acts) [the margin gives Acts xvi, 12–24], [[1:30|and now|et nunc]], when I am bound at Rome, [[1:30|have heard of me|audistis de me]].

paras.t: Porro de prædicto desiderio dissolutionis a corpore, quod non solum Apostolo, sed viris perfectis inest et convenit, dicta sunt multa ad Romanos, super illud : Infelix ego homo! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? Quæ illic requirantur.
paras.en: Further, about the desire just spoken of, to be dissolved from the body, which is found in and befits not only the Apostle but all perfect men, much was said on Romans, upon the words: [[Rom 7:24|Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?|Infelix ego homo! quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus?]] Let it be looked for there.

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : ITAQUE, FRATRES MEI CARISSIMI, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, etc.

paras.t: Consequenter, post exhortationes præhabitas consolatur Apostolus Philippenses. Itaque, id est, quoniam tantam beatitudinem exspectamus et sortituri sumus, o fratres mei carissimi, secundum appetitum superiorem seu intellectualem, id est valde dilecti, quoad futuram felicitatem in patria, et desideratissimi, secundum appetitum inferiorem ac sensitivum, ordinatum et rationi subjectum, id est valde a me desiderati, quoad mutuum conspectum in hac vita : propono enim venire ad vos; gaudium meum materialiter, id est, de quorum profectu et gratia gaudeo, et corona mea, id est augmentum gloriæ meæ in patria, quoniam omnium meritorum vestrorum sum particeps tanquam institutor vester ac doctor ; sic state in Domino, carissimi, id est, constantes atque immobiles estote in Deo, adhærendo justitiæ sicut et ego, ut dicere valeatis illud Job : Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram.
paras.en: Next, after the exhortations already given, the Apostle consoles the Philippians. [[4:1|Therefore|Itaque]], that is, since we await so great a beatitude and are to obtain it, O [[4:1|my dearly beloved brethren|fratres mei carissimi]], according to the higher or intellectual appetite, that is, greatly loved, as regards the future happiness in the fatherland, [[4:1|and most desired|et desideratissimi]], according to the lower and sensitive appetite, ordered and subject to reason, that is, greatly desired by me, as regards seeing one another in this life: for I purpose to come to you; [[4:1|my joy|gaudium meum]] materially [that is, as the matter or occasion of my joy], that is, you at whose progress and grace I rejoice, [[4:1|and my crown|et corona mea]], that is, the increase of my glory in the fatherland, since I share in all your merits as your founder and teacher; [[4:1|so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved|sic state in Domino, carissimi]], that is, be constant and immovable in God, cleaving to justice as I do, so that you may say that word of Job: [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]].

paras.t: Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere, id est idem sentire cum aliis sanctis. in Domino. Has duas devotas matronas exprimit nominatim, quia spectabilis erant vitæ, et fidelibus necessaria ministraverunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|I beg of Evodia and I beseech Syntyche to be of one mind|Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere]], that is, to think the same as the other saints, [[4:2|in the Lord|in Domino]]. He names these two devout matrons expressly, because they were of notable life and ministered necessaries to the faithful.

paras.t: Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar, id est, adjutor et socius meus. Est autem Germanus nomen proprium viri, qui inter Philippenses egregius fuit. Adjuva illas, id est, prælatas feminas conforta in bono, quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio, id est in prædicatione evangelicæ veritatis : non utique prædicando, quoniam mulierem docere non permitto, sed mihi evangelizanti necessaria ministrando ; cum Clemente, id est etiam Clementi, et ceteris adjutoribus meis collaboraverunt, ministrando necessaria eis, sicut et mihi ; quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ, id est, qui ad æternam beatitudinem præordinati sunt, ut confido, vel, ut ex divina revelatione certo scio. Porro, secundum Thomam in prima parte, liber vitæ in Deo metaphorice dicitur. Quemadmodum enim homo eos conscribit qui ad se specialiter pertinent, sic dicitur Deus scripsisse electos qui ad eum finaliter spectant. Unde ipsa electorum conscriptio in mente divina, seu firma eorum notitia in intellectu divino, liber vitæ vocatur, qui aliud prorsus non est nisi prædestinatio Dei. Quum autem dicitur liber vitæ, intelligendum est de vita gloriæ. De hoc libro ait Salvator : Gaudete quod nomina vestra scripta sunt in libro vitæ. Quod vero prædicti scripti fuerint in libro vitæ, Paulus certo scire non potuit nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: [[4:3|And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion|Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar]], that is, my helper and comrade. Now Germanus is the proper name of a man who was eminent among the Philippians [Denis takes *germane*, “genuine”, as a proper name]. [[4:3|help those women|Adjuva illas]], that is, strengthen in good the women aforesaid, [[4:3|who have laboured with me in the gospel|quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio]], that is, in the preaching of the gospel truth: not indeed by preaching, since I suffer not a woman to teach[[1 Tim 2:12||]], but by ministering necessaries to me as I preached the gospel; [[4:3|with Clement|cum Clemente]], that is, they laboured also with Clement [[4:3|and the rest of my fellow labourers|et ceteris adjutoribus meis]], ministering necessaries to them as to me; [[4:3|whose names are in the book of life|quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ]] (Denis reads “are written”), that is, who have been foreordained to eternal beatitude, as I trust, or as I know for certain from divine revelation. Moreover, according to Thomas in the First Part, the book of life is said of God metaphorically. For as a man enrols those who belong to him in a special way, so God is said to have written the elect, who are ordered to him as their end. Hence this enrolment of the elect in the divine mind, or the firm knowledge of them in the divine intellect, is called the book of life, which is nothing else at all than the predestination of God. And when it is called the book of life, it is to be understood of the life of glory. Of this book the Saviour says: Rejoice [[Luke 10:20|that your names are written in heaven|quod nomina vestra scripta sunt]] in the book of life [the margin gives “cf. Luke x, 20”; the Gospel has “in heaven”]. But that the aforesaid were written in the book of life, Paul could not know for certain except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Præterea admonet Apostolus Philippenses ad spiritualem ac jugem lætitiam. Gaudete in Domino semper, id est, in Deo tanquam in objecto, videlicet in contemplatione et dilectione Dei beneficiorumque ejus, imo in omni eo quod Domino placet, spiritualiter exsultate, divinæ perfectioni, majestati ac beatitudini cordialiter congaudendo, de beneficiis quoque ejus nobis collatis sive promissis lætando, et in omni actu virtuoso quo Deus honoratur et colitur, delectando. Signum namque virtutis, est delectatio operis, secundum Philosophum. Semper autem gaudendum est hoc modo, actu vel habitu, seu debitis horis, vel in prosperis et adversis, sicut alibi dicit Apostolus : Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes. Sed gaudium istud, durante præsentis peregrinationis exsilio, non excludit admixtionem omnis tristitiæ. Hoc gaudium fuit in Virgine gloriosa, quæ cecinit : Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo. Non ergo in creaturis gaudendum est, nisi per relationem ad Deum, in quantum earum usus, amor, possessio, vel notitia manuducit ad Deum. Iterum dico, ad excitandum vestræ devotionis affectum, et meæ exhortationis veritatem confirmandum, gaudete in Domino, modo præfato, servientes ei hilariter, imo cum jubilo cordis.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle urges the Philippians to spiritual and constant gladness. [[4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]], that is, exult spiritually in God as in your object, namely in the contemplation and love of God and of his benefits, nay in everything that pleases the Lord: rejoicing from the heart with the divine perfection, majesty and beatitude, being glad also at his benefits bestowed on us or promised, and taking delight in every virtuous act by which God is honoured and worshipped. For the sign of virtue is delight in the work, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle]. And one must always rejoice in this way, in act or in habit, or at due hours, or in prosperity and adversity, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Cor 6:10|As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing|Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes]]. But this joy, while the exile of the present pilgrimage lasts, does not exclude the admixture of every sadness. This joy was in the glorious Virgin, who sang: [[Luke 1:47|And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour|Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo]]. One must not, therefore, rejoice in creatures except by reference to God, in so far as their use, love, possession or knowledge leads us by the hand to God. [[4:4|again, I say|Iterum dico]], to stir up the affection of your devotion and to confirm the truth of my exhortation, [[4:4|rejoice|gaudete]] in the Lord in the manner said, serving him cheerfully, nay with jubilation of heart.

paras.t: Modestia vestra in verbis et factis, id est conversationis vestræ moderatio, discretio, ordinatusque modus, nota sit omnibus hominibus, id est, talis ac tanta sit, ut omnibus innotescat per visum vel famam, ad gloriam Creatoris, et proximorum ædificationem, sicut in Evangelio Dominus loquitur : Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, etc. Dominus prope est, id est paratus ad succurrendum : imo per pietatem et gratiam suam in vobis habitat. Unde et ipse testatur : Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum. Et rursus : Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo. In omnibus quoque est Deus per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam. In ipso etiam vivimus, movemur et sumus. Denique, prope est Deus orantibus et afflictis, juxta illud : Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum ; et, Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Intus est diligentibus, sicut ait Joannes : Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo. Longe est ab impiis, prout in Proverbiis legitur. Propter quod per Jeremiam dicit : Non est anima mea ad populum istum.
paras.en: [[4:5|Let your modesty|Modestia vestra]] in words and deeds, that is, the moderation, discretion and ordered measure of your conduct, [[4:5|be known to all men|nota sit omnibus hominibus]], that is, be such and so great that it becomes known to all by sight or report, to the glory of the Creator and the edification of your neighbours, as the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus]], etc. [[4:5|The Lord is nigh|Dominus prope est]], that is, ready to help: nay, by his kindness and grace he dwells in you. Hence he himself testifies: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]. And again: [[Apoc 3:20|Behold, I stand at the gate and knock. If any man shall hear my voice and open to me the door, I will come in to him and will sup with him|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo]]. God is also in all things by essence, presence and power. In him too we live, and move, and are[[Acts 17:28||]]. Lastly, God is near to those who pray and those afflicted, according to that: [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him|Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum]]; and, [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. He is within those who love him, as John says: [[1 John 4:16|he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]]. He is far from the wicked, as we read in Proverbs[[Prov 15:29||]]. Wherefore he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 15:1|my soul is not towards this people|Non est anima mea ad populum istum]].

paras.t: Nihil solliciti sitis : id est, quum Dominus prope sit, de nulla re angustiari, seu inordinatam curam habere debetis ; sed primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis. Unde et Petrus : Omnem, inquit, sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in Deum, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis ; et Christus, Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum. Omnia hæc de inordinata atque superflua cura, quæ ad diffidentiam quodammodo pertinet, asseruntur : de qua Salomon dicit, Spes sollicitorum peribit. Verumtamen, sicut frequenter præhabitum est, est quædam sollicitudo spiritualis ac ordinata, quæ est diligens animi vigilantia circa bona honesta aut necessaria : quam sæpe commendat præcipitque Scriptura, ut est istud, Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite ; item, Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis.
paras.en: [[4:6|Be nothing solicitous|Nihil solliciti sitis]]: that is, since the Lord is nigh, you ought to be anxious about nothing, or to have inordinate care; but [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis]] (all necessary things, says Denis). Hence Peter too says: [[1 Pet 5:7|Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you|Omnem … sollicitudinem vestram … cura est de vobis]]; and Christ: [[Matt 6:34|Be not therefore solicitous for to morrow|Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum]]. All these things are said of inordinate and superfluous care, which belongs in a way to distrust: of which Solomon says: [[Prov 11:7|the expectation of the solicitous shall perish|Spes sollicitorum peribit]]. Yet, as has often been said before, there is a certain spiritual and ordered solicitude, which is a diligent watchfulness of mind about goods that are honourable or necessary: this Scripture often commends and commands, as in this: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; and again: [[Eph 4:3|Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]].

paras.t: Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum. Hic ponuntur quatuor partes orationis vel species, quarum distinctio est. Oratio enim est simplex precatio, quæ est de facilioribus impetrandis. Obsecratio est invocatio Dei cum commemoratione sacrorum seu divinorum, quorum virtute aut merito aliquid impetrare optamus : sicut quum dicimus, Per passionem tuam, vel, Propter bonitatem tuam, exaudi nos. Estque obsecratio pro difficilioribus obtinendis, ut est justificatio impii. Petitio vero est invocatio Dei pro bonis gratiæ, quæ ordinantur ad bona gloriæ. Alibi quoque ponit Apostolus aliud genus orationis, quod dicitur postulatio, quæ est pro bonis patriæ. Sæpius tamen unum istorum pro alio sumitur. Hortatur ergo Apostolus, ut petitiones nostræ factæ in omni, id est quacumque, oratione et obsecratione et gratiarum actione, ex tanta puritate, attentione et fervore mentis procedant, quatenus apud Deum innotescant, id est a Deo attendantur, et per acceptationem noscantur, atque ab angelis sanctis ei præsententur, quemadmodum in Actibus angelus ait Cornelio : Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei. Et in Paralipomenon libro scriptum est, quod Isaias et Ezechias vociferati sunt usque in cœlum contra Sennacherib, pervenitque oratio eorum ad habitaculum sanctum Dei.
paras.en: [[4:6|but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God|Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum]]. Here four parts or kinds of prayer are set down, between which there is a distinction. For *prayer* is simple entreaty, which concerns obtaining easier things. *Supplication* [Latin *obsecratio*, from *ob sacra*, “by holy things”] is the invocation of God with mention of sacred or divine things by whose power or merit we desire to obtain something: as when we say, By thy passion, or, For thy goodness' sake, hear us. And supplication is for obtaining more difficult things, such as the justification of the ungodly. *Petition* is the invocation of God for the goods of grace, which are ordered to the goods of glory. Elsewhere the Apostle sets down another kind of prayer too, called *postulation*[[1 Tim 2:1||]], which is for the goods of the fatherland. Yet more often one of these is taken for another. The Apostle therefore exhorts that our petitions, made in every, that is, any, prayer and supplication and thanksgiving, should proceed from such purity, attention and fervour of mind that they may be known to God, that is, heeded by God and known by being accepted, and presented to him by the holy angels, as in the Acts the angel says to Cornelius: [[Acts 10:4|Thy prayers and thy alms are ascended for a memorial in the sight of God|Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei]]. And in the book of Paralipomenon it is written that Isaias and Ezechias cried out even to heaven against Sennacherib[[2 Par 32:20||]], and their prayer came to the holy dwelling place of God[[2 Par 30:27||]].

paras.t: Et pax Dei increata, immensa, æterna, id est Deus pacificus, quæ pax exsuperat omnem sensum, id est, omnem intellectum creatum, angelicum et humanum, omnemque gustum et experientiam ejus in infinitum excedit, custodiat effective corda vestra, id est voluntates ab omni prava affectione, et intelligentias vestras, id est intellectum speculativum et practicum omnium vestrum, ab omni errore, in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam et meritum Christi; vel, In Christo Jesu, id est, ut jugiter maneatis in ipso. Vel sic: Pax Dei creata, videlicet tranquillitas mentis a Deo infusa, quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, quoad suam fontalem plenitudinem seu plenam perfectionem; vel, Exsuperat omnem sensum viatorum, secundum quod in patria habetur ac degustatur; custodiat formaliter corda vestra et intelligentias a perturbatione et inquietudine, quatenus pax ista in vobis permaneat, et vitia sibi opposita ab interioribus vestris excludat.
paras.en: [[4:7|And the peace of God|Et pax Dei]], uncreated, immense, eternal, that is, God the peacemaker, [[4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ exsuperat omnem sensum]], that is, which infinitely exceeds every created intellect, angelic and human, and all its taste and experience, [[4:7|keep your hearts|custodiat corda vestra]] effectively [that is, as the efficient cause], that is, your wills from every evil affection, [[4:7|and minds|et intelligentias vestras]], that is, the speculative and practical intellect of all of you, from every error, [[4:7|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace and merit of Christ; or, in Christ Jesus, that is, so that you may abide in him continually. Or thus: the created peace of God, namely tranquillity of mind infused by God, which surpasses all understanding as to its fontal fulness or full perfection; or, surpasses all the understanding of wayfarers, as it is possessed and tasted in the fatherland; keep formally [that is, as the form in the soul itself] your hearts and minds from disturbance and disquiet, so that this peace may abide in you and shut out from your inner parts the vices opposed to it.

paras.t: De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera veritate doctrinæ, vitæ aut justitiæ, quæcumque pudica, id est verba et facta casta, lasciviam excludentia, quæcumque sunt justa quoad proximum, quæcumque sancta quantum ad cultum divinum, quæcumque amabilia, id est, quæ inducunt ad mutuam amicitiam, quæcumque bonæ famæ, id est, quæ bonam famam pariunt et conservant, si qua virtus, id est, quia est aliqua virtus moralis, intellectualis et theologicalis vobis necessaria, si qua laus disciplinæ, id est, quia est aliqua disciplina morum, laudabilis scilicet compositio motuum ac sensuum exteriorum; hæc cogitate assidue, non solum ut sciatis, sed ut ea agendo seu obtinendo, virtuosi salvique sitis, quæ et didicistis ex mea prædicatione, et accepistis per cognitionem intellectivam, et audistis, id est, ab aliis percepistis ea esse in me, et vidistis per experientiam hoc verum esse. Hæc opera virtuosa agite, et Deus dator, amator et conservator pacis internæ, erit vobiscum quotidie per gratiam ampliorem.
paras.en: [[4:8|For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true|De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera]] with the truth of doctrine, of life or of justice, [[4:8|whatsoever modest|quæcumque pudica]], that is, chaste words and deeds that shut out wantonness, [[4:8|whatsoever just|quæcumque justa]] as regards one's neighbour, [[4:8|whatsoever holy|quæcumque sancta]] as regards divine worship, [[4:8|whatsoever lovely|quæcumque amabilia]], that is, things that lead to mutual friendship, [[4:8|whatsoever of good fame|quæcumque bonæ famæ]], that is, things that beget and preserve a good name, [[4:8|if there be any virtue|si qua virtus]], that is, since there is some virtue, moral, intellectual and theological, necessary to you, [[4:8|if any praise of discipline|si qua laus disciplinæ]], that is, since there is a certain discipline of manners, namely a praiseworthy ordering of the outward movements and senses; [[4:8|think on these things|hæc cogitate]] assiduously, not only that you may know them, but that by doing or attaining them you may be virtuous and saved; [[4:9|The things which you have both learned|quæ et didicistis]] from my preaching, [[4:9|and received|et accepistis]] by intellectual knowledge, [[4:9|and heard|et audistis]], that is, learned from others to be [[4:9|in me|in me]], [[4:9|and seen|et vidistis]] by experience to be true: [[4:9|these do ye|Hæc agite]] as virtuous works, [[4:9|and the God of peace shall be with you|et Deus pacis erit vobiscum]]: God, the giver, lover and preserver of inward peace, will be with you daily by more abundant grace.

paras.t: Insuper congratulatur Apostolus liberalitati Philippensium, non principaliter ob proprium emolumentum, sed propter illorum caritatem ac meritum. Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando, id est post tempora longa, refloruistis, id est, more arboris iterum floruistis, seu fructuose viguistis et convaluistis, pro me sentire, et meæ inopiæ compati atque succurrere, sicut et ante sentiebatis pro me. Occupati autem eratis negotiis aliis : idcirco excusabiles estis de tanta dilatione refloritionis istius.
paras.en: Moreover the Apostle congratulates the Philippians on their liberality, not chiefly for his own profit, but because of their charity and merit. [[4:10|Now I rejoice in the Lord exceedingly that now at length|Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando]], that is, after a long time, [[4:10|your thought for me hath flourished again|refloruistis pro me sentire]], that is, you have blossomed again like a tree, or thrived and grown strong fruitfully, in thinking for me, and in sympathizing with and relieving my need, [[4:10|as you did also think|sicut et sentiebatis]] for me before. [[4:10|but you were busied|Occupati autem eratis]] with other affairs: therefore you are excusable for so long a delay in this reflowering.

paras.t: Non quasi propter penuriam dico, id est, non ex necessitudine paupertatis meæ hæc assero, ut sustentetur a vobis. Ego enim didici, per gratiam Dei et consuetudinem exercitii mei, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse, id est, quid mihi sufficiat. Natura quippe paucis minimisque contenta est. Scio et humiliari, id est actum humilitatis, tribulationis seu paupertatis prompte et discrete exsequi, scio et abundare, id est in abundantia temporalium non excedere (ubique et in omnibus exercitiis virtutum institutus, id est bene instructus, sum): sciens videlicet et satiari sine immoderantia, et esurire sine impatientia, et abundare, non tamen cor rebus caducis apponere, et penuriam pati in victu ac vestibus sine tristitia. Omnia hæc possum, non propriis viribus, sed in eo qui me confortat, id est per adjutorium Christi. Verumtamen bene fecistis: id est, quamvis donis vestris possem carere, tamen bene et caritative egistis, communicantes, id est eleemosynam vestram impertientes, tribulationi meæ, id est mihi incarcerato atque afflicto.
paras.en: [[4:11|I speak not as it were for want|Non quasi propter penuriam dico]], that is, I do not say this out of the need of my poverty, that I may be supported by you. [[4:11|For I have learned|Ego enim didici]], by the grace of God and the custom of my practice, [[4:11|in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith|in quibus sum, sufficiens esse]], that is, what suffices me. For nature is content with few and very small things. [[4:12|I know both how to be brought low|Scio et humiliari]], that is, to carry out promptly and discreetly the act of humility, of tribulation or of poverty, [[4:12|and I know how to abound|scio et abundare]], that is, not to go to excess in an abundance of temporal things [[4:12|(every where and in all things I am instructed)|(ubique et in omnibus institutus sum)]] in the exercises of the virtues, that is, well taught: knowing, namely, [[4:12|both to be full|et satiari]] without immoderation, [[4:12|and to be hungry|et esurire]] without impatience, [[4:12|both to abound|et abundare]] yet not set the heart on perishable things, [[4:12|and to suffer need|et penuriam pati]] in food and clothing without sadness. [[4:13|I can do all things|Omnia possum]], not by my own strength, but [[4:13|in him who strengtheneth me|in eo qui me confortat]], that is, by the help of Christ. [[4:14|Nevertheless, you have done well|Verumtamen bene fecistis]]: that is, though I could do without your gifts, yet you have acted well and charitably, [[4:14|in communicating|communicantes]], that is, imparting your alms, [[4:14|to my tribulation|tribulationi meæ]], that is, to me imprisoned and afflicted.

paras.t: Præterea præfert Apostolus Philippenses aliis, quantum ad aliquid, quatenus laudibus suis auditis, provocentur ad meliora. Virtus enim laudata, augetur in bonis. Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii, id est illo tempore prædicationis meæ evangelicæ, quando profectus sum, id est recessi, a Macedonia, verbo prædicationis illic disseminato, nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit, id est, temporalia dedit, in ratione dati et accepti, id est in rationabili recompensatione temporalium, pro exhibitione spiritualium quæ vobis communicavi : rationis enim censura hoc dictat, ut spiritualia bona præstanti seu dispensanti, temporalia ministrentur ; nisi vos soli : in quo declaratur gratitudo ac liberalitas vestra ; quia et Thessalonicam, id est ad urbem sic dictam, semel et bis, id est tribus vicibus, vel semel et iterum, in usum, id est ad utendum, mihi misistis temporalia vestra, ut necessaria vitæ ex eis acciperem. Non quia quæro datum, id est, non ideo vos commendo quia munera vestra requiro, sed requiro fructum abundantem, id est meritum copiosum, in ratione vestra jam dicta, videlicet in rationabili recompensatione qua mihi temporalia pro spiritualibus communicatis. Habeo autem omnia quæ misistis, et abundo in eis, ita ut aliis indigentibus ea communicem. Repletus sum gaudio mentis et copia rerum, acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis mihi, odorem suavitatis, id est, quæ sic placent Deo ut odor suavissimus. Eleemosyna namque est hostia Deo gratissima. Ideo sequitur : hostiam acceptam, Deo placentem. Unde ad Hebræos ait : Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle sets the Philippians above others in a certain respect, so that, hearing their own praises, they may be stirred to better things. For virtue praised grows in the good. [[4:15|And you also know, O Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel|Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii]], that is, at that time of my gospel preaching, [[4:15|when I departed|quando profectus sum]], that is, withdrew, [[4:15|from Macedonia|a Macedonia]], the word of preaching having been sown there, [[4:15|no church communicated with me|nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit]], that is, gave temporal things, [[4:15|as concerning giving and receiving|in ratione dati et accepti]], that is, in reasonable recompense of temporal things for the spiritual things I imparted to you: for the judgment of reason dictates this, that temporal things be ministered to him who furnishes or dispenses spiritual goods[[1 Cor 9:11||]][[Rom 15:27||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor ix, 11–13 and Rom xv, 27]; [[4:15|but you only|nisi vos soli]]: in which your gratitude and liberality are shown; [[4:16|For unto Thessalonica also|quia et Thessalonicam]], that is, to the city so called, [[4:16|you sent once and again|semel et bis]], that is, three times, or once and a second time, [[4:16|for my use|in usum]], that is, to be used, your temporal goods, that I might take from them the necessaries of life. [[4:17|Not that I seek the gift|Non quia quæro datum]], that is, I do not commend you because I seek your gifts, [[4:17|but I seek the fruit that may abound|sed requiro fructum abundantem]], that is, copious merit, [[4:17|to your account|in ratione vestra]] already mentioned, namely in the reasonable recompense by which you impart to me temporal things for spiritual. [[4:18|But I have all|Habeo autem omnia]] that you sent, [[4:18|and abound|et abundo]] in them, so that I share them with others in need. [[4:18|I am filled|Repletus sum]] with joy of mind and plenty of things, [[4:18|having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent|acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis]] me, [[4:18|an odour of sweetness|odorem suavitatis]], that is, things which so please God as a most sweet odour. For alms is a sacrifice most pleasing to God. Therefore it follows: [[4:18|an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God|hostiam acceptam, placentem Deo]]. Hence he says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:16|And do not forget to do good and to impart: for by such sacrifices God's favour is obtained|Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus]].

paras.t: Deus autem meus impleat, id est, exaudiat et operi mancipet, omne desiderium vestrum rationabile et sincerum, secundum divitias suas in gloria, id est pie, gratiose et copiose, secundum quod ipse in se dives est in gloria, id est in beatitudine sua. Vel, Impleat desiderium vestrum in gloria, dando videlicet vobis gloriam sempiternam; in Christo Jesu, id est per Dominum Salvatorem, et per gratiam seu meritum ejus. Deo autem per creationem, et Patri nostro per gubernationem, videlicet summæ et incommutabili Trinitati, sit gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
paras.en: [[4:19|And may my God supply|Deus autem meus impleat]], that is, hear and bring to effect, [[4:19|all your want|omne desiderium vestrum]] [Latin *desiderium*, “desire”], reasonable and sincere, [[4:19|according to his riches in glory|secundum divitias suas in gloria]], that is, kindly, graciously and abundantly, according as he is himself rich in glory, that is, in his beatitude. Or, may he fulfil your desire in glory, namely by giving you everlasting glory; [[4:19|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the Lord the Saviour, and through his grace or merit. [[4:20|Now to God|Deo autem]] by creation, [[4:20|and our Father|et Patri nostro]] by governance, namely to the supreme and unchangeable Trinity, be [[4:20|glory, world without end. Amen|gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen]].

paras.t: Salutate, id est, salutem optate ac dicite, omnes sanctos ad vestram societatem spectantes, in Christo Jesu, id est secundum Christi doctrinam, vel ut in Christo permaneant. Salutant vos qui mecum sunt fratres, id est cooperatores ac socii mei. Salutant vos omnes sancti in Urbe morantes, maxime autem qui de domo Cæsaris sunt, id est ministri Neronis quos converti, qui et specialem dilectionem ad vos gerunt.
paras.en: [[4:21|Salute ye|Salutate]], that is, wish and speak salvation to, [[4:21|every saint|omnem sanctum]] (Denis reads “all the saints”) belonging to your fellowship, [[4:21|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, according to Christ's teaching, or that they may abide in Christ. [[4:22|The brethren who are with me salute you|Salutant vos, qui mecum sunt, fratres]], that is, my fellow workers and companions. [[4:22|All the saints salute you|Salutant vos omnes sancti]], dwelling in the City, [[4:22|especially they that are of Caesar's household|maxime autem qui de Cæsaris domo sunt]], that is, servants of Nero whom I have converted, who also bear a special love towards you.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro, id est, in anima vestra, perficiendo ejus essentiam. Amen, id est, sic fiat atque præstetur vobis a Deo sublimi et benedicto.
paras.en: [[4:23|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro]], that is, in your soul, perfecting its essence. [[4:23|Amen|Amen]], that is, so be it done and granted to you by God most high and blessed.
